title: Retraining and Model Maintenance
learning_outcomes: Explain retraining and model maintenance and accurately refer to at least two syllabus subtopics.
Apply the main idea of retraining and model maintenance to a small example, trace, calculation, or scenario.
Identify one important assumption or failure mode and describe how to check it.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study retraining and model maintenance in the context of production data science and mlops. You will connect the PDF subtopics to a small example and practice describing what the evidence does—and does not—support.
content.why_it_matters: Retraining and Model Maintenance matters because it affects how data is collected, represented, analyzed, interpreted, or used in a decision. Check the task and assumptions before choosing a method.

content_blocks.title: The central idea
content_blocks.text: Production data science joins model artifacts to tested software, deployment, monitoring, access control, and rollback. Offline performance does not guarantee reliable real-world behavior.

items.title: Retraining triggers
items.text: Define retraining triggers in relation to retraining and model maintenance; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

items.title: Scheduled versus event-driven retraining
items.text: Work through scheduled versus event-driven retraining using a small, synthetic example before scaling up. State what the calculation or method returns and why that result is useful.

items.title: Training-data freshness
items.text: Check the edge cases for training-data freshness: missing values, unusual ranges, different groups, time boundaries, or a changed input can affect the conclusion.

items.title: Comparing replacement models
items.text: Document the rule or choice for comparing replacement models so another learner can reproduce the analysis and understand its limitations.

items.title: Rollback and retirement procedures
items.text: Define rollback and retirement procedures in relation to retraining and model maintenance; identify the input, output, assumptions, and who uses the result.

content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the provided synthetic input, rerun or retrace the example, and change one value at a time. Do not use personal records, credentials, or data you are not authorized to access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Keep the question, data grain, units, and assumptions explicit. If a result differs, inspect the input and steps in order. Avoid turning an observed association into a causal claim, treating a sample as the population, or assuming a small demonstration guarantees production behavior. Simple drift indicators require thresholds, valid reference windows, and investigation before automatic action.

content_blocks.title: Responsible interpretation
content_blocks.text: This example is a teaching aid. It is static in the CodeLeaf lesson and is not executed in the browser. It uses small synthetic values; validate any real workflow in a separate, appropriate local environment and protect sensitive data.

content_blocks.title: Recap and next step
content_blocks.text: Recap: Production data science joins model artifacts to tested software, deployment, monitoring, access control, and rollback. Offline performance does not guarantee reliable real-world behavior. Next, connect this lesson to the linked prerequisite or following lesson. Record the method, input assumptions, observed result, and one limitation so another person can reproduce and review the work.

task_acceptance_criteria: Refer accurately to the topic and its syllabus subtopics.
Record a reproducible example or a complete manual trace with an expected result.
Document at least one assumption, limitation, data-quality issue, or evaluation check.
hints: Write down the input, expected result, units, and assumptions first.
Change only one condition when testing a revised example.
Ask whether the data and method represent the real decision; do not infer causality or production readiness from a toy example.
troubleshooting: Check input values, path assumptions, package versions, indentation, and units.
For SQL, use a local schema and read-only test data; this page does not provide a live database.
For package-dependent work, create an isolated environment and use the relevant official documentation.
